application_guidance.input_pattern: An ONS run on a fixed compact convex decision set with known positive alpha,G,D and exact metric projection.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic and uniform over the stated loss sequences.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The displayed Regret bound has explicit constants. O(n^2) describes dense arithmetic only; no bit-complexity constant is asserted.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact current-loss gradient at x_t; exact A_t-metric projection is a separately charged capability.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible online decisions x_t and static-comparator cumulative loss Regret R_T; no final optimization error or dynamic Regret claim.
complexity_scope.regime: n,T>=1 integers; alpha,G,D>0; exact Figure 3 tuning. No support restriction on decisions beyond membership in P.
complexity_scope.resource: T gradient evaluations suffice; at most T-1 metric projections for T decisions, or T when terminal x_{T+1} is formed. O(n^2) dense update arithmetic and storage, excluding both gradient and projection costs (§3.2.1).
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper performance bound for deterministic ONS, Figure 3; not a lower bound over an Algorithm class.

map: p.11 Lemma 3: h=exp(-2 beta f) is concave since 0<2 beta<=alpha. Its tangent inequality gives f(x)>=f(y)-(1/(2 beta))log(1-2 beta grad f(y)^T(x-y)). Since |2 beta grad f(y)^T(x-y)|<=2 beta GD<=1/4 and -log(1-z)>=z+z^2/4 for |z|<=1/4, obtain f(x)>=f(y)+grad f(y)^T(x-y)+(beta/2)(grad f(y)^T(x-y))^2.
p.12 Eq.(3): take x=x* minimizing the total loss and y=x_t. Then f_t(x_t)-f_t(x*)<=g_t^T(x_t-x*)-(beta/2)(g_t^T(x_t-x*))^2.

p.26 Lemma 8: with z the exact projection of y, optimality gives (z-y)^T A(a-z)>=0. Expanding the difference of squared distances yields ||y-a||_A^2-||z-a||_A^2>=(y-z)^T A(y-z)>=0. This applies with A=A_t positive definite and a=x*.
p.12 Eqs.(4)–(6) expand y_{t+1}=x_t-beta^(-1)A_t^(-1)g_t and use Lemma 8: g_t^T(x_t-x*) <= g_t^T A_t^(-1)g_t/(2 beta)+(beta/2)[||x_t-x*||_{A_t}^2-||x_{t+1}-x*||_{A_t}^2].

p.13: summing that recursion, A_t-A_{t-1}=g_t g_t^T cancels the negative quadratic terms from Eq.(3). Drop the nonpositive terminal distance. The remaining initial contribution is (beta/2)||x_1-x*||_{A_0}^2 <= beta epsilon D^2/2=1/(2 beta), yielding the first inequality in the statement.

pp.30–32 Lemmas 11–12: for A>=B>0, trace(A^(-1)(A-B))<=log(det A/det B), obtained from C=A^(-1/2) B A^(-1/2) and sum_i[1-lambda_i(C)]<=-sum_i log lambda_i(C). With A=A_t, B=A_{t-1}, telescope to sum_t g_t^T A_t^(-1)g_t<=log(det A_T/det A_0). The largest eigenvalue of A_T is at most epsilon+TG^2 and det A_0=epsilon^n, giving n log(1+TG^2/epsilon). p.13 and first lines p.14 combine this with the initial contribution. Stop before the log(T) simplification.

assumptions: For each t=1,...,T, f_t is twice differentiable and convex, as in §2.2, and exp(-alpha f_t(x)) is concave on P.
For every t=1,...,T and every x in P, ||grad f_t(x)||_2<=G.
Decisions precede revelation of the current loss; gradients and generalized projections in the displayed update are exact.
The same P, alpha, G and D apply throughout. No strong-convexity constant or Hessian lower bound is assumed.
statement.conclusion: R_T <= (1/(2 beta)) sum_{t=1}^T g_t^T A_t^(-1)g_t + 1/(2 beta) <= [1+n log(1+TG^2/epsilon)]/(2 beta) = [1+n log(1+TG^2 beta^2 D^2)]/(2 beta). These are the pre-simplification Proof inequalities on pp.13–14, not the printed simplified Theorem 2 formula.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let P subset R^n be nonempty closed bounded and convex, D=max_{x,y in P}||x-y||_2>0. Let scalar losses f_t:P->R be as below; log is natural. Define beta=0.5 min{1/(4GD),alpha}, epsilon=1/(beta^2 D^2), A_0=epsilon I_n. Start at arbitrary x_1 in P. At each round set g_t=grad f_t(x_t), A_t=A_{t-1}+g_t g_t^T, y_{t+1}=x_t-beta^(-1)A_t^(-1)g_t, x_{t+1}=argmin_{x in P}(x-y_{t+1})^T A_t(x-y_{t+1}). Define R_T=sum_t f_t(x_t)-min_{x in P}sum_t f_t(x).
statement.parameter_domains: n,T positive integers; 0<D<infinity, 0<G<infinity, 0<alpha<infinity; beta and epsilon are the positive values above. Cases D=0 or G=0 are excluded from this parameterization; no separate extension is submitted.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer n>=1, every integer T>=1, every P and alpha,G>0 satisfying the conditions, every admissible sequence f_1,...,f_T and every x_1 in P, the deterministic Figure 3 iterates satisfy the conclusion. No stochastic averaging or failure probability; the argument applies to each realized admissible loss sequence.
